newsitem.title: YEMEN: Yemen minister visits Saudi Arabia on border row.
newsitem.headline: Yemen minister visits Saudi Arabia on border row.

text.p: A Yemeni envoy left for Saudi Arabia on Monday to arrange for a planned visit to the kingdom by Yemeni leader Ali Abdullah Saleh, an official source said.
Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Abdul-Karim al-Iryani would also discuss ties between the two neighbour states trying to settle a 61-year-old border dispute.
The official Yemeni news agency said he was carrying a letter from Saleh to King Fahd.
"Dr Iryani is expected to discuss necessary arrangements for the expected visit of President Saleh to Saudi Arabia in the coming period," the official source told Reuters. He set no date.

Iryani's trip is the first high-level visit to Saudi Arabia since Saleh appointed a new government earlier this month after April general elections, the Arab state's first since a 1994 civil war nearly tore the country apart.
Saleh met King Fahd last summer to speed up talks to settle the border row.
Yemen has hinted in recent months it might resort to international arbitration if more than a year of talks with Riyadh failed to settle the dispute.
Saudi Arabia and Yemen had several minor clashes in a border area potentially rich in oil and gas before the two sides signed a memorandum of understanding in 1995 to resolve the dispute.
A joint committee looking into border demarcation has met scores of times since 1995.

Yemen's relations with Gulf Arab states, including Saudi Arabia, have improved in the last few years. Sanaa angered its Gulf Arab neighbours when it appeared to side with Iraq during the 1990-91 Gulf crisis over Iraq's invasion of Kuwait.
